key_insight: A symmetry-aware variational framework can simulate the finite-size Dicke model on both qubit-only and hybrid qubit-boson quantum platforms while recovering Dicke critical behavior in the large-spin limit.
engineering_relevance: This work points to more resource-efficient quantum simulation pathways for collective light-matter systems on near-term hardware, especially trapped-ion and hybrid quantum devices.
method: Developed a variational simulation of the finite-size Dicke model for digital qubit-based quantum computers.
Introduced a hybrid qubit-bosonic ansatz that directly uses bosonic degrees of freedom to reduce quantum resources.
Designed the framework to be compatible with classical emulators and hardware execution, with symmetry awareness to improve scalability.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the model reproduces the Dicke model’s characteristic critical behavior in the appropriate large-spin limit and was tested on both classical emulators and trapped-ion quantum computers.
watch_item: Hardware execution on current trapped-ion devices is still limited by noise, which may constrain accuracy and scalability.
paper_title: Simulating the Dicke Model on Qubit-Based and hybrid Qubit-Boson-Based Quantum Computers
